properties.description:
reflow2-mcp has its own `rocksdb` feature (on-disk storage, a design store in a folder), ON BY DEFAULT, so every build anyone installs or runs has it: a release (release.yml), `cargo install`, the Docker images (docker/build.sh), the installer's source-build line and the launcher all build with default features. `cargo dev-test`, a cargo alias in .cargo/config.toml, builds and tests both crates without it on the in-memory backend; librocksdb-sys is not in that build's dependency graph at all. `cargo full-test` is CI's full run.

A build without the feature REFUSES every store in a folder, first and before anything is opened, locked or written, naming the build, the feature and the fix (`opening::refuse_without_on_disk_storage`, the core's fail-loud contract and error kind in this crate's terms). It is asked by the two openers every mode goes through (ReflowService::new_reporting, one_shot::open_store), by `--shared` (which would otherwise start a daemon that can only fail) and by `--export-snapshot`. A server says it in band on the degraded surface; nothing falls back to memory.

The crate's test files are compiled into four test programs instead of one each (`autotests = false`): `in_memory` (every file whose tests need no store; a disk test inside one is marked `#[cfg(feature = "rocksdb")]`), `on_disk` (every file all of whose tests open a store; `required-features = ["rocksdb"]`), and two that need a process of their own (mint_seat_liveness: a one-way process-wide latch; a_design_is_watched_at_the_server_that_holds_it: it sets REFLOW2_CONFIG_DIR process-wide). Every file keeps its path and is a module, so its tests are `<file>::<test>`. `every_test_file_runs_in_exactly_one_program` fails a file declared in no program. tools/run_to_files.py reads such a program per test, so each file is still reported on its own.

CI's core job (no RocksDB) builds, tests and lints the crate without the feature so that configuration cannot rot; the full job is unchanged and runs every test, with RocksDB, on every pull request.
properties.name: Everyday builds and tests run without RocksDB, every installed server keeps it, and the server's tests are four test programs
